title: Tiny SDK Probe Patterns and Handoff Notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact, pragmatic onramp for small language SDKs (mobile and microservice-focused) we want product and solutions teams to use for first-10-minute success. It focuses on three things: a lean quickstart flow, reliable minimal telemetry/telemetry contract for observability, and a short handoff checklist for engineering pairs to ship.

Audience:
- SDK maintainers and integrators
- Developer advocates and solutions engineers preparing customer demos
- Oncall / SRE who need minimal signals to triage SDK-based incidents

Context / problem statement:
We keep getting internal ask: "I want to show a demo in <10 minutes and not worry about keys, logs, or token costs." The full starter guides are long and include a lot of choices (auth modes, batching, retry strategies). For quick adoption we need a tiny, opinionated path: a one-file quickstart, a sample app pattern (single-file serverless + tiny web page), and a minimal telemetry contract that surfaces the three signals SREs ask for.

High-level quickstart (1-2 minute flow):
1) Pre-reqs: 1) API key (create from Console) 2) node 18+ installed or Python 3.10+ 3) git
2) Clone a single-file starter: `git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/tiny-sdk-probe && cd tiny-sdk-probe`
3) Create .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY and optional REGION. Example provided in repo.
4) Run `npm run start` or `python -m tiny_probe` — server will start on localhost:3000 and show a tiny web UI that calls the SDK.
5) Open browser, paste prompt, press send. Walkthrough demonstrates streaming, cost meter, and an error-simulate toggle.

One-file quickstart examples (concise):
- Node: minimal fetch wrapper, 10 lines to call Redwood text generation endpoint with streaming handler.
- Python: single script using requests + SSE parsing helper to print incremental tokens.
- Curl: explicit example showing how to set Authorization header, content-type, and a short prompt.

Developer patterns we want to promote (opinionated):
- Single-entrypoint pattern: expose `client.generate(prompt, opts)` from the tiny library, keep default token limit reasonable (512), and explicit opt-in for larger contexts.
- Fail-open fallback: on 429 or transient service error, retry once with exponential backoff, but surface a clear telemetry event (see contract).
- Local-mode simulation: include a small `--local-sim` flag that uses canned responses so demos can run without network.

Minimal telemetry contract (3 required signals):
1) SDK.request_start and SDK.request_end events (trace id included)
   - Fields: trace_id, model_name, tokens_requested_est, mode (stream|non-stream), region_hint
2) SDK.error event when request fails after any retry
   - Fields: trace_id, http_status, error_code, duration_ms, user_facing (true|false)
3) SDK.cost_approx event when response completes
   - Fields: trace_id, tokens_out, tokens_in, approximate_cost_usd

Format / transport guidance:
- Emit to stdout in JSON for local/demo runs (so devs can see events).
- In production OSS SDKs, wire to the existing telemetry abstraction (Telemetry.emit) and map to our internal ingestion (if present) but default to no remote telemetry unless configured.
- Provide helper that attaches trace_id to outgoing HTTP headers: `X-RDWD-TRACE` so server-side logs can correlate.

Error surface & common pitfalls (short):
- Missing API key: quickstart should show a clear console message with the exact console URL to create a key.
- Streaming partial tokens only: show a checkbox in UI to toggle streaming vs buffered so demoers can point out difference.
- Costs spike: default tiny demo environment should cap tokens and display a live cost estimate.

Sample handoff checklist for demos or customer POC:
- [ ] Confirm small starter repo runs in under 5 minutes locally without network (use --local-sim).
- [ ] Add example .env with placeholder key and link to Console for key create flow.
- [ ] Ensure telemetry stdout displays SDK.request_start/end events for every request in demo mode.
- [ ] Document where to change model_name and token caps (one variable at top of file).
- [ ] Add a one-paragraph README that explains failure modes and how to escalate to eng-sre (link to ENG-4821).

Onboarding script for solutions engineers (3 steps):
1) Walk through the tiny quickstart locally, show streaming and cost meter.
2) Demonstrate the fallback path by toggling error-simulate and show telemetry event that appears on stdout.
3) If customer wants reserved capacity, show where in code to pin model_version and how to set routing_policy to dedicated. (Provide snippet and link to Console route docs.)

Rollout notes and gating for inclusion in official SDK repo:
- Keep tiny quickstart as a separate top-level directory `examples/tiny-probe` to keep it extremely lightweight.
- Add a small e2e test that runs the local-sim path in CI and validates telemetry events are emitted.
- Gate: merge when e2e passes and README includes cost-warning and telemetry mapping section.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should telemetry events include customer_id by default in demos? (privacy concern — recommend NO, opt-in only).
- How opinionated should the cap on default tokens be? (Proposal: 512 default for tiny probe).
- Should the tiny quickstart include a minimal server-side component that demonstrates `X-RDWD-TRACE` propagation? (Proposal: yes, single express route)

Next steps (owner: Maya Patel):
- Spin up tiny example repo scaffold and push initial commit (ETA: 1 week).
- Draft short PR template for examples that enforces the telemetry contract (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Coordinate with solutions-eng to rehearse the 5-minute demo (ETA: 3 weeks).

Notes to self / breadcrumbs:
- Related internal ticket: ENG-4821 (telemetry mapping).
- Reference quick demos: slack thread #sdk-onramp/threads/CF9Y2
- Keep handoff lean — customers appreciate "run this in 5 minutes" more than a long tutorial.

-- end of note --
